## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The fire and the coolness  (`#the-fire-and-the-coolness`)

Cited ayat: 21:68-70, 29:24, 37:97-98

> **21:68** قَالُوا۟ حَرِّقُوهُ وَٱنصُرُوٓا۟ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ فَٰعِلِينَ
>
> **21:69** قُلْنَا يَٰنَارُ كُونِى بَرْدًا وَسَلَٰمًا عَلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ
>
> **21:70** وَأَرَادُوا۟ بِهِۦ كَيْدًا فَجَعَلْنَٰهُمُ ٱلْأَخْسَرِينَ

> **29:24** فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُوا۟ ٱقْتُلُوهُ أَوْ حَرِّقُوهُ فَأَنجَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَٰتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ

> **37:97** قَالُوا۟ ٱبْنُوا۟ لَهُۥ بُنْيَٰنًا فَأَلْقُوهُ فِى ٱلْجَحِيمِ
>
> **37:98** فَأَرَادُوا۟ بِهِۦ كَيْدًا فَجَعَلْنَٰهُمُ ٱلْأَسْفَلِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (21:68): His people said: burn him, and help your gods, if you are going to act.

**c2** (29:24): In another passage the only answer of his people was to say: kill him, or burn him.

**c3** (37:97): In another passage they said: build a structure for him, and throw him into the blaze.

**c4** (21:69): God told the fire to be coolness and safety for Ibrahim.

**c5** (21:70): They wanted to plot against him, and God made them the greatest losers.

**c6** (37:98): In another passage God made them the lowest.

**c7** (29:24): God saved him from the fire, and in that, God says, are signs for people who believe.

### One-minute summary

His people said to burn Ibrahim [c1][c2], but God told the fire to be coolness and safety for him [c4]. They wanted to plot against him, and God made them the losers [c5][c7].

### Complete story

His people said: burn him, and help your gods, if you are going to act [c1]. In another passage their only answer was to say: kill him, or burn him [c2], and in another they said: build a structure for him, and throw him into the blaze [c3].

God told the fire to be coolness and safety for Ibrahim [c4]. They wanted to plot against him, and God made them the greatest losers [c5]; in another passage He made them the lowest [c6]. God saved him from the fire, and in that, He says, are signs for people who believe [c7].

### Deep study

The passages report the people's decision in slightly different words: burn him [c1], kill him or burn him [c2], build a structure and throw him into the blaze [c3]. The words said to the fire come in one passage only [c4], and the outcome is told in different words, greatest losers and lowest [c5][c6]. The rescue is stated in one passage, with a remark that it contains signs [c7].

### Kids mode

Ibrahim's people said to burn him [c1]. God told the fire to be cool and safe for Ibrahim [c4]. God saved him from the fire [c7].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage presents the fire as acting only at God's word [c4]. Another is that the plot of Ibrahim's people ends in their own loss [c5].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: where this took place, how long the fire burned, or who built the structure.
- The verses state the command to the fire and the rescue; they do not describe Ibrahim in the fire or how he came out of it.
- Not established: whether the passages (21:68-70, 29:24, 37:97-98) describe one decision or more than one; this draft reads them together as the same event.
- Not established: how the structure and the blaze of 37:97 relate to the fire of the other passages.
